newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita Elec says worried over Asia forex woes.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita Elec says worried over Asia forex woes.

text.p: The head of business in Asia and Oceania for Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd said on Tuesday that the currency crisis in Asia may affect the firm's domestic market-oriented units in Thailand and the Philippines.

Asked about the impact of recent sharp falls in the Thai baht and the Philippine peso on Matsushita's business, Katsuro Sakakibara, director of Matsushita's Corporate Management Division for Asia and Oceania, said manufacturing costs at its affiliate National Thai Co would rise by several percent.
He said the firm, owned 49 percent by Matsushita, would be forced to rationalise its manufacturing process or raise its product prices.
Sakakibara added, however: "The overall situation (in Thailand) will not be so bad," because another unit reliant on exports would benefit from the currency's fall.

In the Philippines, Matsushita owns three units. Two of them are used as bases for exports from the Philippines, but the third, Matsushita Philippines, is oriented towards the domestic market and will have to increase sales prices due to the impact of the fall in the currency, he said.
Sakakibara said he was worried that the currency problem in Asia could create many problems in Asian economies, such as high interest rates, inflation and a weakening in consumers' purchasing power.
"We are not expecting a big slump, but we are concerned that the speed of the economies' growth in the Asian area will be slowed down," he said.

He also said exports from Matsushita in Japan to Asian markets in the April-June quarter would be "reasonably good" but added that he was still keeping a cautious stance because of the currency falls.

He said Matsushita had been planning to set up a new company to transfer the manufacture of "white" goods, or large domestic appliances such as refrigerators and washing machines, from National Thai Co to a new joint venture in Thailand, but because of the currency problem it was reviewing the feasibility of the plan.
